column3: MT 69:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. Close to the Hebrew; “On Shoshannim” is translated as “The Lilies,” and NKJV adds “A Psalm.”
Close to the Hebrew; “what I did not steal, then I must restore” is rendered “Though I have stolen nothing, I still must restore it.”
Close to the Hebrew; וְאַשְׁמוֹתַי (“my guilt”) is rendered “my sins.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I wept with fasting my soul” is rendered “I wept and chastened my soul with fasting.”
Close to the Hebrew; “taunt songs of drinkers of strong drink” is rendered “the song of the drunkards.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a time of favor” is rendered “the acceptable time,” and “faithfulness” “truth.”
Close to the Hebrew; וָאָנוּשָׁה (“I am sick”) is rendered “I am full of heaviness,” and “to show sympathy” “to take pity.”
Close to the Hebrew; רֹאשׁ (“poison, gall”) is rendered “gall.”
NKJV renders וְלִשְׁלוֹמִים (“for their allies / peace offerings”) as “their well-being,” and swaps “trap” and “snare.”
Close to the Hebrew; טִירָתָם (“their encampment”) is rendered “their dwelling place.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the scroll of life” is rendered “the book of the living.”
